entities.summary:
George Kodinos, also known as Pseudo-Kodinos or Codinus, was a late Byzantine author active during the 15th century. He is best recognized for his 16th-century manuscript, the 'De Re Militari,' which remains a valuable source of information on medieval military tactics and technology.

Born in Constantinople around 1410, Kodinos served as a military engineer and military officer in the Byzantine Empire before transitioning to writing. His literary output, while not extensive, has been instrumental in shaping the understanding of Byzantine military strategies and the development of early modern warfare.

Despite the scarcity of information on his personal life, Kodinos' works have been studied extensively by historians and scholars, offering unique insights into the military practices and technological advancements of the late Byzantine period.

Kodinos' legacy continues to be felt among historians and military strategists, as his writings remain a crucial component of understanding the evolution of warfare from the Byzantine Empire to the early modern era.

'In the realm of military science, Kodinos' treatise stands as a testament to the ingenuity and resourcefulness of the Byzantine people in the face of adversity.'
